title: Cut to the Mix: Simple Data Augmentation Outperforms Elaborate Ones in Limited Organ Segmentation Datasets
mechanism: Supervised CutMix between labelled images (box ~ Beta(0.5,0.5)) with labels copied, compared with CarveMix, AnatoMix and ObjectAug on small data.
adaptation: CutMix between two labelled train cells of the same cell type, box aligned to the cell grid; labels follow the box; 50% of batches; no mixing across BMRK and others at first (label width differs). Seams are labelled from both sides, teaching that discontinuities are not cracks.
min_experiment: PF+CM vs PF, 5 seeds; mIoU_rob, splice/gridline/edge_dark/material IoU, crack IoU and false crack px on 31 crack-free val cells. Kill: mIoU_rob < +0.005 and crack IoU change within +-0.012.
evidence: 20 training CT volumes (AMOS), 16 organs, nnU-Net: CutMix +4.8 macro Dice with TDA (78.2 to 83.0), CarveMix +2.5, AnatoMix +3.2, ObjectAug collapsed to 22.6 macro.
prior_overlap: Partial: CutMix was run inside Mean Teacher on the unlabelled stream (n.d. at 100%). Supervised CutMix of labelled cells never run.
